newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: LUXEMBOURG CLAMPS DOWN ON MONEY LAUNDERING.
newsitem.headline: LUXEMBOURG CLAMPS DOWN ON MONEY LAUNDERING.

text.p: Luxembourg Justice Minister Marc Fischbach on Wednesday unveiled a draft law to crack down on money laundering and make the financial sector take a greater role in informing authorities of suspicious transactions.
The government said it would toughen the sentencing of money laundering offences, which until recently only made drug money laundering punishable by imprisonment.
The new law will make association with criminals, including in the financial sector, trafficking and possession of illegal weapons and immoral behaviour bear harsher punishments.
The government added that the new law would force the financial sector, insurance firms, solicitors and accountants to inform appropriate authorities of any indications of money laundering.
Money laundering, according to the new law, would only be a criminal offence for the person who knowingly committed it.
Accomplices who could not be proved to have known of the crime would no longer be considered as money launderers.
The new law, adopted by the government last Friday, should come into force by the end of the year.
